content: Itraconazole is a medication used to treat a variety of fungal infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as azole antifungals. Before starting itraconazole, it is important to read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This should also be done each time you receive a refill. Take this medication orally with a full meal, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. If you are taking antacids, take itraconazole two hours before or one hour after the antacids, as antacids can reduce the absorption of this medication. If you have low or no stomach acid (achlorhydria) or are taking medications that reduce stomach acid (such as H2 blockers like ranitidine or proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole), take itraconazole with an acidic drink, such as cola, to improve absorption. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. It is crucial to take this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For optimal effectiveness, take itraconazole at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) every day. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the infection to return. Itraconazole is available in different forms, such as capsules, tablets, and solutions, which may deliver varying amounts of the medication and may be used for different purposes. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, stomach upset, or dizziness. If these effects persist or worsen, contact your doctor promptly. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, itraconazole can cause serious (possibly fatal) liver disease. It may also cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it can be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that may indicate a severe allergic reaction. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare, but if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Before taking itraconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other azole antifungals (such as ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Itraconazole may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages, and consult your doctor if you are using marijuana. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Itraconazole should not be used to treat fungal nail infections if you are pregnant or could become pregnant during treatment. Women of childbearing age should start this medication 2 to 3 days after the start of their menstrual period to ensure they are not pregnant. Itraconazole passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Itraconazole interacts with many medications. Other drugs may affect the removal of itraconazole from your body, which could impact its effectiveness. If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests) should be performed before starting this medication and periodically while taking it. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for more details on how to safely discard your product. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
